hook: Doctors give patients a thick drink of barium sulfate before an X-ray of the gut. Barium ions are toxic, so why is this safe? Barium sulfate dissolves so little that a liter of water holds only a few thousandths of a gram of it. An equilibrium constant, K<sub>sp</sub>, tells you exactly how little.

prereq.q: What does "soluble" mean for an ionic compound in water?
options: An appreciable amount dissolves to form ions
It does not dissolve at all
It reacts with water to form a gas
prereq.why: Soluble salts dissolve and dissociate into ions.

prereq.q: When CaCl<sub>2</sub> dissolves, how many Cl<sup>−</sup> ions form per formula unit?
Which species are left out of an equilibrium constant expression?
prereq.why: Their concentrations are fixed, so they drop out.

figure.caption: Write each ion concentration as s times its coefficient, then solve K<sub>sp</sub> for s. Square the whole 2s.

chain.cause: A slightly soluble salt is placed in water
chain.effect: ions leave the solid, and some return to it

chain.cause: Ions return as fast as they leave
chain.effect: the saturated solution is at equilibrium, with K<sub>sp</sub> = product of ion concentrations

chain.cause: Each formula unit releases ions in the ratio of its formula
chain.effect: every ion concentration is s times its coefficient

chain.cause: The ion concentrations are put into K<sub>sp</sub> with their exponents
chain.effect: you can solve for s, or calculate K<sub>sp</sub> from a measured s

chain.cause: The ion product Q is greater than K<sub>sp</sub>

ideas: Ksp is the product of the ion concentrations in a saturated solution, each raised to its coefficient; the solid is left out.
Molar solubility s: mol of salt dissolved per liter. 1 : 1 salt: Ksp = s². MX2 salt: Ksp = s(2s)² = 4s³.
Rank solubility by K<sub>sp</sub> only for salts with the same ion ratio.
Q > K<sub>sp</sub>: precipitate forms. Q < K<sub>sp</sub>: more can dissolve.

misconception.wrong: For Mg(OH)₂, K<sub>sp</sub> = s × 2s, because there are two hydroxide ions.
misconception.right: [OH⁻] = 2s, and it is raised to the power 2 in K<sub>sp</sub>: K<sub>sp</sub> = s(2s)² = 4s³. Forgetting to square [OH⁻] is the most common Ksp error on the exam.

summary: A slightly soluble salt reaches a dynamic equilibrium with its ions in a saturated solution. K<sub>sp</sub> is the product of the ion concentrations, each raised to its coefficient, with the solid left out. Writing each ion as s times its coefficient links K<sub>sp</sub> to the molar solubility s (s² for a 1 : 1 salt, 4s³ for a 1 : 2 or 2 : 1 salt). Compare K<sub>sp</sub> values directly only for salts with the same ion ratio; Q above K<sub>sp</sub> means a precipitate forms.
